decisions.quote: Changes in bench press velocity and power after 8 weeks of high-load cluster- or traditional-set structures [57] | Non-significant | 0.304 | 0.129 | 1.07 | 0.14 | Compatible | Inconclusive (neither significantly different from the null nor the original)
decisions.reason: The target identity is resolved to Davies et al. (2020) [57], which Murphy et al. (2025) re-tested in a new sample (type: replication). Under Rule 1, the authors' target-specific overall verdict governs. In Table 6, the authors explicitly classify the overall replication outcome for [57] as 'Inconclusive (neither significantly different from the null nor the original)' because the replication NHST result was non-significant while the Z-test found the replication effect size (0.129) statistically compatible with the original effect size (0.304; z = 1.07, p = 0.14). This contradicts the shipped 'failed' coding, as the authors explicitly distinguish 'Inconclusive' from both 'Informative failure to replicate' and 'Practical failure to replicate'. At the same time, the codebook forbids coding 'uninformative' merely because an estimate is nonsignificant or imprecise without a stated study-specific defect preventing adjudication (and Table 7, containing study-specific quality notes, is absent from the source text). Accordingly, as noted in the blind coding ('cannot_be_determined'), no substantive codebook outcome category is supported and the field is undeterminable.
